content:
maya: quick follow-ups from today's runtime Q&A thread - dropping them here so owners can respond.
liam: ready.
sandra: can we get a clearer ship window for the scheduler refactor? slide said 'next quarter' which is a bit fuzzy for planning.
carlos: working target: internal canary mid-April, broader canary late-April, full rollout May. still chasing a couple micro-regressions.
jen: what kind of regressions are we seeing? p95/p99 or correctness?
carlos: primarily tail latency for tiny sequences when batching thresholds align poorly; no correctness issues.
ashley: could you paste a tiny repro log so folks can run local sim?
carlos: sure:
```
2026-04-10T09:21:02Z serve WARN batch_scheduler.cpp:198 - dropped_batch_count=3 max_batch=32 got=36
2026-04-10T09:21:02Z runtime INFO kernel_scheduler.cpp:57 - microbatch_assignments=[4,4,4,4,4,6]
```
noah: is that on optimized-kernels or main?
carlos: optimized-kernels branch. kernel latency changed microbatch packing heuristics.
liam: rollout mechanics: will this be a global flip or per-pool opt-in?
maya: per-pool opt-in for Dedicated/Private; hosted will be staged with automatic fallback on SLO breach.
sandra: will we expose a simulated cost/latency impact before teams flip?
ashley: Console plan: sim against historical traces, show delta for p50/p95/cost. not auto-apply.
carlos: ops note: we'll add a compatibility flag so older agent versions keep previous scheduler until they opt in.
jen: caching question: any change to KV cache semantics? time-based TTLs?
carlos: default remains LRU by capacity; we'll add optional TTL plugin for customers who want time-based eviction.
noah: if a kernel change increases p99 for some customers by >5%, do we have automated rollback?
maya: yes - hosted uses default thresholds with automatic fallback; Dedicated/Private have opt-in thresholds and can enable auto-rollback.
sandra: can Product publish recommended SLO thresholds folks should use for chat vs embeddings?
maya: will coordinate, target doc by next week.
liam: CI ask: can the perf harness emit a canary marker so pipelines detect regressions?
carlos: adding `--canary` flag to harness this week.
ashley: could we also get a small checklist for running the harness locally? many infra folks asked.
carlos: README update coming: example command `./harness --model llama-13b --seq-distribution short --canary`.
deploy-bot: Rollout planned: kernel-scheduler-v2 -> canary pools mid-April. See /deploys/198 for details.
jen: thanks, that helps.
liam: propose a 20-minute follow-up with eng-runtime next Tue 10am PT to walk through the checklist and canary plan.
maya: scheduled. I'll drop calendar invite. :calendar:
